```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "caret",
  "pROC"
)

new_packages <- required_packages[!(required_packages %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]

if (length(new_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(new_packages)
}

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
```

# 1. Introduction

This R Markdown document presents the K-Nearest Neighbour model used to predict customer recommendation behaviour for Gelugor Fashion Store. The target variable is `recommend_index`, where customers are classified as either `Recommend` or `Not_Recommend`. The `Not_Recommend` class is treated as the positive class because it represents loyalty-risk customers who may require targeted improvement actions.

# 2. Load Dataset

```{r load-data}
final_ml_dataset <- read_csv("final_ml_dataset.csv")

dim(final_ml_dataset)
str(final_ml_dataset)
head(final_ml_dataset)
```

## Target Distribution

```{r target-distribution}
table(final_ml_dataset$recommend_index)
prop.table(table(final_ml_dataset$recommend_index))
```

# 3. Data Preparation for KNN

The target variable is converted into a factor with two classes: `Not_Recommend` and `Recommend`. Character predictors are converted into factors. Since KNN is distance-based, categorical predictors will later be converted into dummy variables.

```{r data-preparation}
knn_data <- final_ml_dataset %>%
  mutate(
    recommend_index = factor(
      ifelse(recommend_index == 1, "Recommend", "Not_Recommend"),
      levels = c("Not_Recommend", "Recommend")
    ),
    across(where(is.character), as.factor),
    feedback_count_group = as.factor(feedback_count_group)
  )

table(knn_data$recommend_index)
prop.table(table(knn_data$recommend_index))
str(knn_data)
```

# 4. Train-Test Split

The dataset is divided into 80% training data and 20% testing data using stratified sampling. This helps preserve the class distribution of `Recommend` and `Not_Recommend` in both datasets.

```{r train-test-split}
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  knn_data$recommend_index,
  p = 0.8,
  list = FALSE
)

knn_train_raw <- knn_data[train_index, ]
knn_test_raw  <- knn_data[-train_index, ]

dim(knn_train_raw)
dim(knn_test_raw)

table(knn_train_raw$recommend_index)
table(knn_test_raw$recommend_index)
```

# 5. Dummy Encoding

KNN requires numeric predictors because it calculates distance between observations. Therefore, categorical variables are converted into dummy variables using `dummyVars()`.

```{r dummy-encoding}
knn_train_predictors <- knn_train_raw %>%
  select(-recommend_index)

knn_test_predictors <- knn_test_raw %>%
  select(-recommend_index)

dummy_model <- dummyVars(
  ~ .,
  data = knn_train_predictors,
  fullRank = TRUE
)

knn_train_x <- predict(dummy_model, newdata = knn_train_predictors) %>%
  as.data.frame()

knn_test_x <- predict(dummy_model, newdata = knn_test_predictors) %>%
  as.data.frame()

colnames(knn_train_x) <- make.names(colnames(knn_train_x), unique = TRUE)
colnames(knn_test_x) <- make.names(colnames(knn_test_x), unique = TRUE)

knn_train_y <- knn_train_raw$recommend_index
knn_test_y  <- knn_test_raw$recommend_index

dim(knn_train_x)
dim(knn_test_x)
```

# 6. Remove Near-Zero Variance Features

Near-zero variance features contain very little useful information and may reduce model stability. These features are removed before training the KNN model.

```{r remove-nzv}
nzv_cols <- nearZeroVar(knn_train_x)

length(nzv_cols)

if (length(nzv_cols) > 0) {
  knn_train_x <- knn_train_x[, -nzv_cols, drop = FALSE]
  knn_test_x  <- knn_test_x[, -nzv_cols, drop = FALSE]
}

dim(knn_train_x)
dim(knn_test_x)
```

# 7. KNN Parameter Tuning

A 10-fold cross-validation method is used to tune the KNN model. The number of neighbours, `k`, is tested from 3 to 101 using odd values. The model is optimized based on ROC. Range normalization is applied because KNN is sensitive to differences in variable scale.

```{r knn-tuning}
knn_control <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

knn_grid <- expand.grid(
  k = seq(3, 101, by = 2)
)

set.seed(123)

knn_model <- train(
  x = knn_train_x,
  y = knn_train_y,
  method = "knn",
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = knn_control,
  tuneGrid = knn_grid,
  preProcess = c("range")
)

print(knn_model)
knn_model$bestTune
```

## KNN Tuning Plot

```{r knn-tuning-plot}
plot(knn_model)

knn_tuning_plot <- ggplot(knn_model$results, aes(x = k, y = ROC)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "KNN Parameter Tuning Using 10-Fold Cross-Validation",
    x = "Number of Neighbours (k)",
    y = "ROC (Cross-Validation)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

knn_tuning_plot

ggsave(
  "KNN_TuningPlot.png",
  knn_tuning_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# 8. Test Set Prediction

The trained KNN model is applied to the test dataset. Both predicted classes and predicted probabilities are generated.

```{r prediction}
knn_pred <- predict(knn_model, newdata = knn_test_x)
knn_prob <- predict(knn_model, newdata = knn_test_x, type = "prob")

head(knn_pred)
head(knn_prob)
```

# 9. Confusion Matrix

The confusion matrix is used to evaluate how many customers were correctly and incorrectly classified. The positive class is set as `Not_Recommend` because this group represents loyalty-risk customers.

```{r confusion-matrix}
knn_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  data = knn_pred,
  reference = knn_test_y,
  positive = "Not_Recommend"
)

print(knn_cm)
```

## Save Confusion Matrix Table

```{r save-confusion-matrix}
knn_cm_table <- as.data.frame(knn_cm$table)

knn_cm_table

write_csv(knn_cm_table, "KNN_ConfusionMatrix_Table.csv")
```

## Confusion Matrix Heatmap

```{r confusion-matrix-plot}
knn_cm_plot <- ggplot(knn_cm_table, aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = Freq,
      colour = ifelse(Freq > max(Freq) / 2, "white", "black")
    ),
    size = 6
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#FEE8C8",
    high = "#E6550D"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "KNN Confusion Matrix",
    x = "Actual Class",
    y = "Predicted Class",
    fill = "Freq"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

knn_cm_plot

ggsave(
  "KNN_ConfusionMatrix.png",
  knn_cm_plot,
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# 10. ROC Curve and AUC

The ROC curve evaluates how well the KNN model separates `Not_Recommend` and `Recommend` customers. A higher AUC value indicates stronger classification separability.

```{r roc-auc}
knn_roc <- roc(
  response = knn_test_y,
  predictor = knn_prob$Not_Recommend,
  levels = c("Recommend", "Not_Recommend")
)

knn_auc <- auc(knn_roc)

knn_auc
```

## ROC Curve Plot

```{r roc-plot}
plot(
  knn_roc,
  main = paste("KNN ROC Curve, AUC =", round(knn_auc, 3))
)

png("KNN_ROC.png", width = 1000, height = 800, res = 150)

plot(
  knn_roc,
  main = paste("KNN ROC Curve, AUC =", round(knn_auc, 3))
)

dev.off()
```

# 11. Save KNN Performance Metrics

The model performance is summarized using Accuracy, Kappa, Balanced Accuracy, Recall, Specificity, Precision, F1-score and AUC. Since the business focus is identifying loyalty-risk customers, Recall for `Not_Recommend` and Balanced Accuracy are especially important.

```{r save-metrics}
knn_metrics <- data.frame(
  Model = "K-Nearest Neighbour",
  Accuracy = as.numeric(knn_cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
  Kappa = as.numeric(knn_cm$overall["Kappa"]),
  Balanced_Accuracy = as.numeric(knn_cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]),
  Recall_NotRecommend = as.numeric(knn_cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
  Specificity_Recommend = as.numeric(knn_cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
  Precision_NotRecommend = as.numeric(knn_cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]),
  F1_NotRecommend = as.numeric(knn_cm$byClass["F1"]),
  AUC = as.numeric(knn_auc),
  Best_k = knn_model$bestTune$k,
  Removed_NZV_Features = length(nzv_cols)
)

knn_metrics

write_csv(knn_metrics, "KNN_Metrics.csv")
```

# 12. Save Final Model

The final KNN model is saved as an RDS file so that it can be reused later for prediction or model deployment.

```{r save-model}
saveRDS(knn_model, "KNN_Model.rds")
```

# 13. Conclusion

The K-Nearest Neighbour model was developed to predict whether customers would recommend a clothing item. KNN is useful as a distance-based classification model, but its performance depends strongly on scaling, dummy encoding and the selected value of `k`. The final model should be evaluated based on Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Recall for `Not_Recommend`, Precision, F1-score and AUC. Since `Not_Recommend` customers represent loyalty-risk customers, the model is especially useful only if it can correctly detect this class.
